audioscript.text: On behalf of LP clubs, I'd like to welcome you all here today.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: My name is Sandy Fisher, and I'm one of the fitness managers here.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Before we start our tour of the club, I'll just run through some basic information about the facilities we have here, including recent improvements, and explain the types of membership available.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Our greatest asset is probably our swimming pool, which at 25 meters isn't Olympic sized, but now we've expanded it to eight lanes, it's much wider.

audioscript.text: Section 4, you will hear a university lecture about an endangered bear in British Columbia, Canada, known as the spirit bear.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Today we continue our series on ecology and conservation with a look at a particularly endangered member of the black bear family.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: One in 10 black bears is actually born with a white coat, which is the result of a special gene that surfaces in a few.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q31: The passage says the white coat is *'the result of a special gene'* — **'result of'** means **'comes from'**. So the answer is **gene**.

audioscript.text: Local people have named it the spirit bear, and according to the legends of these communities, its snowy fur brings with it a special power.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q32: The passage says its fur *'brings with it a special power'* — **'unusual'** in the question means **'special'**. So the answer is **power**.

audioscript.text: Because of this, it has always been highly regarded by them, so much that they do not speak of seeing it to anyone else.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: It is their way of protecting it when strangers visit the area.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q33: The passage says they protect it *'when strangers visit the area'* — they protect the bear **from** these people. So the answer is **strangers**.

audioscript.text: The white bear's habitat is quite interesting.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The bear's strong relationship with the old growth rainforest is a complex one.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The white bear relies on the huge centuries old trees in the forest in many ways.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: For example, the old growth trees have extremely long roots that help prevent erosion of the soil along the banks of the many fish streams.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q34: The passage says tree roots *'help prevent erosion of the soil'* — **'stop'** in the question means **'prevent'**. So the answer is **erosion**.

audioscript.text: Keeping these banks intact is important, because these streams are home to salmon, which are the bear's main food source.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: In return, the bears' feeding habits nurture the forest.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: As the bears eat the salmon, they discard the skin and bones in great amounts on the forest floor, which provide vital nutrients.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: These produce lush vegetation that sustains thousands of other types of life forms.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: From birds to insects and more.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Today, the Spirit bear lives off the coast of the province of British Columbia on a few islands.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q35: The passage says the bear *'lives off the coast... on a few islands'* — **'currently found on'** means **'lives on'**. So the answer is **islands**.

audioscript.text: There is great concern for their survival.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Since it is estimated that less than 200 of these white bears remain.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The best way to protect them is to make every effort to preserve the delicate balance of their forest environment.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: In other words, their ecosystem.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The greatest threat to the bear's existence is the loss of its habitat.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Over many years, logging companies have stripped the land by cutting down a large number of trees.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: In addition, they have built roads which have fractured the areas where the bear usually feeds, and many hibernation sites have also been lost.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q36: The passage says logging companies *'have built roads'* — this is the **construction** mentioned in the question. So the answer is **roads**.

audioscript.text: The logging of the trees along the streams has damaged the places where the bears fish.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: To make matters worse, the number of salmon in those streams is declining, because there is no legal limit on fishing at the moment.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q37: The passage says *'there is no legal limit on fishing'* — **'no legal limit'** means **'unrestricted'**. So the answer is **fishing**.

audioscript.text: All these influences have a negative impact on the spirit bear's very existence, which is made all the more fragile by the fact that reproduction among these bears has always been disappointingly low.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q38: The passage says *'reproduction among these bears has always been disappointingly low'* — **'low rate of'** in the question matches **'disappointingly low'**. So the answer is **reproduction**.

audioscript.text: And so, what's the situation going forward?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Community organizations, environmental groups, and the British Columbia government are now working together on the problem.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The government is now requiring logging companies to adopt a better logging method, which is a positive step.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q39: The passage says companies must *'adopt a better logging method'* — **'improve their'** in the question means **'adopt a better'**. So the answer is **method**.

audioscript.text: However, these measures alone may not be sufficient to ensure a healthy population of the spirit bear in the future.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Other steps also need to be taken.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: While it is important to maintain the spirit bear's habitat, there also needs to be more emphasis on its expansion.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q40: The passage says there needs to be *'more emphasis on its expansion'* — **'maintenance and'** in the question connects to **'maintain'** and **'expansion'**. So the answer is **expansion**.

audioscript.text: The move is justified.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: As it will also create space for other bears that are losing their homes...
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That is the end of Section 4.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Section 2, you will hear a representative of a city council giving information about two new facilities which are opening soon in the city.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Good morning.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: I'm very pleased to have this opportunity to say a little about two exciting new developments in the city.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The Brackenside Open-air Swimming Pool, and the children's adventure playground in Central Park.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: As many of you may know, the idea for these initiatives came from you, the public, in the extensive consultation exercise which the City Council conducted last year.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q11: The passage says the idea *'came from you, the public'* — **'the public'** means **'local people'**. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: And they have been realized using money from the SWRDC - the South West Regional Development Commission.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: First of all, Brackenside Pool.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: As many of the older members of the audience will remember, there used to be a wonderful open air pool on the seafront 30 years ago, but it had to close when it was judged to be unsafe.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: For the design of this new heated pool, we were very happy to secure the talents of internationally renowned architect, Ellen Wendon, who has managed to combine a charming 1930s design which fits so well with many of the other buildings in the area.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: With up to the minute features such as a recycling system, the only one of its kind in the world, which enables seawater to be used in the pool.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q12: The passage says the pool has a *'recycling system, the only one of its kind in the world, which enables seawater to be used'* — this is a special **method of water treatment**. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Now.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: There's been quite a bit of discussion in the local press about whether there would be enough room for the number of visitors we're hoping to attract, but the design is deceptive, and there have been rigorous checks about capacity.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q13: The passage says local press discussed *'whether there would be enough room for the number of visitors'* — **'enough room'** means **'the size of the facilities'**. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Uh. Also just in case you were wondering, we're on schedule for June 15th opening date, and well within budget, a testimony to the excellent work of local contractors Hickman's.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: We hope that as many people as possible will be there on June 15th.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: We have engaged award winning actress Coral White to declare the pool open, and there'll be drinks and snacks available at the poolside.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: There'll also be a competition for the public to decide on the sculpture we plan to have at the entrance.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q14: The passage says there will be a *'competition for the public to decide on the sculpture'* and *'which famous historical figure'* to have — this means the **statue at the door** is not yet chosen. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: You will decide which famous historical figure from the city we should have.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q14: The passage says there will be a *'competition for the public to decide on the sculpture'* and *'which famous historical figure'* to have — this means the **statue at the door** is not yet chosen. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 15 to 20.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 15 to 20.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: And now, moving on to the Central Park playground, which we're pleased to announce has just won the Douglas Award for safety.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The news came through only last week.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The unique design is based on the concept of the Global Village, with the playground being divided into six areas showing different parts of the world, each with a representative feature.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: For example, there is a section on Asia, and this is represented by rides and equipment in the shape of snakes, orangutans, tigers, and so on - fauna native to the forests of the region.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q15: The passage says Asia is represented by *'snakes, orangutans, tigers... fauna native to the forests'* — **'fauna'** means **'local animals'**. So the answer is **E**.

audioscript.text: Moving south to the Antarctic, we couldn't run to an ice rink, I'm afraid, but opted instead for climbing blocks in the shape of mountains.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q16: The passage says for Antarctica they *'opted instead for climbing blocks in the shape of mountains'* — this directly matches **mountains**. So the answer is **F**.

audioscript.text: I thought they could have had slides for the glaciers, but the designers did want to avoid being too literal.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Then onto South America, and here the theme is El Dorado, games replicating the search for mines full of precious stones, and then moving up to North America.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q17: The passage says South America's theme is *'El Dorado, games replicating the search for mines full of precious stones'* — **'precious stones'** means **'jewels'**. So the answer is **D**.

audioscript.text: Here there was considerable debate.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: I know the contribution of cinema and jazz was considered, but the designers finally opted for rockets and the International Space Station.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q18: The passage says for North America designers *'opted for rockets and the International Space Station'* — this is **space travel**. So the answer is **H**.

audioscript.text: Eastwards to Europe then, and perhaps the most traditional choice of all the areas, medieval castles and other fortifications, then last but not least, moving south to Africa.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q19: The passage says Europe has *'medieval castles and other fortifications'* — **'fortifications'** means **'ancient forts'**. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: And a whole set of wonderful mosaics and trails to represent the great rivers of this fascinating and varied continent.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q20: The passage says Africa has *'mosaics and trails to represent the great rivers'* — **'rivers'** means **'waterways'**. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: Now, the opening date for our Global Playground is the 10th of July. And again, we'd love to see you there.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So, make a date and come and see this magnificent original new amenity right in the heart of the city.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That is the end of Section 2.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Good morning. Welcome to the Early Learning Childcare Centre. How may I help you?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: Hi. I spoke to you last week about enrolling my daughter to next year.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: Oh, yes. I'll just get some details from you. So, you're her mother?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: That's right.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: And, can I have your name?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: It's Carol, Carol Smith.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: And your daughter's name?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: It's Kate.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: Now, we have several groups at the centre and we cater for children from three to five years old. How old is your daughter?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: She's three now but she turns four next month.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: I'll put four down because that's how old she'll be when she starts.
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR
audioscript.explain: Q1: The director says *'I'll put four down because that's how old she'll be when she starts'* — so the age on the form is **4**, not her current age of three.

audioscript.text: Fine, she's so excited about her birthday and coming to the centre.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: That's good to hear. And what's your address?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: It's 46 Wombat Road, that's WOMBAT. Woodside 4032.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL
audioscript.explain: Q2: The mother gives the address as *'46 Wombat Road'* — the question asks for the address, so the answer is **46 Wombat**.

audioscript.text: And what's the phone number?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: So, have you decided on the days you'd like to bring your daughter here?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: I'd prefer Monday and Wednesday if possible.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: Mmm. I'll check, Monday's fine, but I think the centre is already full for Wednesday. Erm. Yes. Sorry. It seems to be a very popular day. We can offer you a Thursday or a Friday as well.
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: Oh dear. I suppose Thursday would be all right because she has swimming on Friday.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL
audioscript.explain: Q3: The mother first wants Wednesday, but the director says it's full and offers Thursday or Friday. The mother then says *'Thursday would be all right'* — so the day enrolled is **Thursday**.

audioscript.text: OK, got that. Because a lot of parents work, we do offer flexible start and finish times. We are open from 7:30 in the morning until 6 o'clock at night. What time would you like your daughter to start?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: I need to get to work in the city by 9:00 so I'll drop her off at 8:30 . You're pretty close to the city here so that should give me plenty of time to get there.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL
audioscript.explain: Q4: The mother says *'I'll drop her off at 8:30'* — **'drop her off'** means the start time. So the answer is **8:30**.

audioscript.text: That's fine. Now, we also need to decide which group she'll be in. we have two different groups and they're divided up according to age. There's the green group. Which is for three- to four-year-olds. And then there's the red group which is for four- to five-year-olds.
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: She's quite mature for her age and she can already write her name and read a little.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: Well, I'll put her in the red group and we can always change her to the green one if there are any problems.
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR
audioscript.explain: Q5: The director says *'I'll put her in the red group'* — this is the group for four- to five-year-olds. So the childcare group is the **red** group.

audioscript.text: That sounds fine.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: OK. Let's move on to meals. We can provide breakfast, lunch and dinner. As she's finishing pretty early, she won't need dinner, will you give her breakfast before she comes?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: Yes, she'll only need lunch.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL
audioscript.explain: Q6: The director asks about meals, and the mother says *'she'll only need lunch'* — so the meal required each day is **lunch**.

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 7 to 10.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now, does she have any medical conditions we need to know about? Does she have asthma or any hearing problems for example?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: No. But she does need to wear glasses.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL
audioscript.explain: Q7: The director asks about medical conditions, and the mother says *'she does need to wear glasses'* — so the medical condition is **glasses**.

audioscript.text: Oh, I'll make a note of that.
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: Yes, she's pretty good about wearing them, she can't see much without them.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: Right. OK. Now, I also need emergency contact details.
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: So what sort of information do you need?
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: Just the name and number of a friend or family member we can contact in case we can't get hold of you at any time.
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: OK. That'd better be my sister... Jenny Ball . That's BALL. Her phone number is 3346 7523.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL
audioscript.explain: Q8: The mother gives the emergency contact as *'Jenny Ball'* and spells it *'BALL'* — so the last name is **BALL**.

audioscript.text: Great. So she is the child's aunt?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR
audioscript.explain: Q9: The director asks *'she is the child's aunt?'* and the mother confirms — so the relationship to the child is **aunt**.

audioscript.text: Yes, that's right.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: I'll make a note of that as well. Now, is there anything you'd like to ask?
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: What about payment? How much are the fees each term?
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: Well, for two days and the hours you've chosen, that will be $450 altogether.
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: OK, and do I have to pay that now?
audioscript.speaker: CAROL

audioscript.text: No, we send out invoices once the children start at the centre. You can choose to pay at the end of each term or we do offer a slightly discounted rate if you pay every month.
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: Oh, I'll do that then. I find it easier to budget that way and I'm not used to the term dates just yet.
audioscript.speaker: CAROL
audioscript.explain: Q10: The mother chooses to pay every month, saying *'I'll do that then'* after the director offers a monthly option — so she will pay each **month**.

audioscript.text: Good, it makes it a lot simpler for us as well. Well, that's everything. Would you like me to show you around the centre?...
audioscript.speaker: DIRECTOR

audioscript.text: That is the end of section 1.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.

audioscript.text: Section 2, you will hear a woman called Alice Bussell talking on the radio about the Dolphin Conservation Trust, an organization which tries to protect dolphins.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 15.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Today we're pleased to have on the show Alice Bussell from the Dolphin Conservation Trust.
audioscript.speaker: INTERVIEWER

audioscript.text: Uh. Tell us about the trust, Alice.
audioscript.speaker: INTERVIEWER

audioscript.text: Well, obviously, its purpose is to protect dolphins in seas all around the world.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: It tries to raise people's awareness of the problems these marine creatures are suffering because of pollution and other threats.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: It started 10 years ago, and it's one of the fastest growing animal charities in the country.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Although it's still fairly small compared with the big players in animal protection, we're particularly proud of the work we do in education.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Last year, we visited a huge number of schools in different parts of the country.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Going round to talk to children and young people, aged from 5 to 18.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: In fact, about 35% of our members are children.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: The charity uses its money to support campaigns, for example, for changes in fishing policy and so forth.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain:
Q11: The passage says the charity *'uses its money to support campaigns, for example, for changes in fishing policy'* — this means it helps **finance** campaigns. It also says *'many people give their services on a voluntary basis'* and volunteers work in *'observation, office work, and other things'* — this means volunteers help in **various ways**. So the correct answers are **C** and **E**.

Q12: The passage says the charity *'uses its money to support campaigns, for example, for changes in fishing policy'* — this means it helps **finance** campaigns. It also says *'many people give their services on a voluntary basis'* and volunteers work in *'observation, office work, and other things'* — this means volunteers help in **various ways**. So the correct answers are **C** and **E**.

audioscript.text: It hopes soon to be able to employ its first full-time biologist with dolphin expertise to monitor populations.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Of course, many people give their services on a voluntary basis, and we now have volunteers working in observation, office work, and other things.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain:
Q11: The passage says the charity *'uses its money to support campaigns, for example, for changes in fishing policy'* — this means it helps **finance** campaigns. It also says *'many people give their services on a voluntary basis'* and volunteers work in *'observation, office work, and other things'* — this means volunteers help in **various ways**. So the correct answers are **C** and **E**.

Q12: The passage says the charity *'uses its money to support campaigns, for example, for changes in fishing policy'* — this means it helps **finance** campaigns. It also says *'many people give their services on a voluntary basis'* and volunteers work in *'observation, office work, and other things'* — this means volunteers help in **various ways**. So the correct answers are **C** and **E**.

audioscript.text: I should also tell you about the award we won from the Charity Commission last year, for our work in education.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Although it's not meant an enormous amount of money for us, it has made our activities even more widely publicized and understood.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain: Q13: The passage says the award *'has made our activities even more widely publicized and understood'* — **'publicized'** means **'better known'**. So Alice is pleased because it made the trust's work **better known**. The answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: In the long term, it may not bring in extra members, but we're hoping it'll have this effect.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Is it possible to see dolphins in UK waters?
audioscript.speaker: INTERVIEWER

audioscript.text: Yes, in several locations, and we have a big project in the east part of Scotland.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: This has long been a haven for dolphins, because it has very little shipping.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: However, that may be about to change soon, because oil companies want to increase exploration there.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: We're campaigning against this, because although there'll be little pollution from oil,
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: exploration creates a lot of underwater noise.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain: Q14: The passage says *'exploration creates a lot of underwater noise'* — this directly tells you the problem is **noise**. ***Don't be tricked by 'oil leaks'*** — the passage says there will be *'little pollution from oil'*. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: It means the dolphins can't rest and socialize.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: This is how I became interested in dolphin conservation in the first place.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: I had never seen one, and I hadn't been particularly interested in them at school.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Then I came across this story about a family of dolphins who had to leave their home in the Moray Firth.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain: Q15: The passage says Alice *'came across this story'* and *'couldn't put the book down'* — **'couldn't put the book down'** means she was very interested in a **book**. So she became interested when she **read a book** about them. The answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Because of the oil companies, and about a child who campaigned to save them.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: I couldn't put the book down.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain: Q15: The passage says Alice *'came across this story'* and *'couldn't put the book down'* — **'couldn't put the book down'** means she was very interested in a **book**. So she became interested when she **read a book** about them. The answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: I was hooked.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 16 to 20.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 16 to 20.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: I'm sure our listeners will want to find out what they can do to help.
audioscript.speaker: INTERVIEWER

audioscript.text: You mentioned the 'Adopt a Dolphin' scheme.
audioscript.speaker: INTERVIEWER

audioscript.text: Can you tell us about that?
audioscript.speaker: INTERVIEWER

audioscript.text: Of course, people can choose one of our dolphins to sponsor.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: They receive a picture of it, and news updates.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: I'd like to tell you about four, which are currently being adopted by our members.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Moondancer, Echo, Kiwi, and Samson.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Unfortunately, Echo is being rather elusive this year, and hasn't yet been sighted by our observers.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain: Q16: The passage says *'Echo is being rather elusive this year, and hasn't yet been sighted'* — **'hasn't yet been sighted'** means it **has not been seen**. So the comment matches **Echo**. The answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: But we remain optimistic that he'll be out there soon.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: All the others have been out in force.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Samson and Moondancer are often photographed together, but it's Kiwi who's our real character, as she seems to love coming up close for the cameras, and we've captured her on film hundreds of times.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain: Q17: The passage says *'it's Kiwi who's our real character, as she seems to love coming up close for the cameras, and we've captured her on film hundreds of times'* — this means Kiwi is **photographed more** than the others. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: They all have their own personalities.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Moondancer is very elegant and curves out and into the water very smoothly, whereas Samson has a lot of energy.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: He's always leaping out of the water with great vigor.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain: Q18: The passage says *'Samson has a lot of energy'* and *'He's always leaping out of the water with great vigor'* — **'great vigor'** means **very energetic**. So the comment matches **Samson**. The answer is **D**.

audioscript.text: You'd probably expect him to be the youngest, he's not quite, that's Kiwi, but Samson's the latest of our dolphins to be chosen for the scheme.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain: Q19: The passage says *'Samson's the latest of our dolphins to be chosen for the scheme'* — **'latest'** means **the newest one**. So the comment matches **Samson**. The answer is **D**.

audioscript.text: Kiwi makes a lot of noise, so we can often pick her out straight away.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Echo and Moondancer are noisy too, but Moondancer is easy to find, because she has a particularly large fin on her back.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE
audioscript.explain: Q20: The passage says *'Moondancer is easy to find, because she has a particularly large fin on her back'* — a **'particularly large fin'** is an **unusual shape**. So the comment matches **Moondancer**. The answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: Which makes her easy to identify.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: So, yes, they're all very different.
audioscript.speaker: ALICE

audioscript.text: Well, they sound a fascinating group...
audioscript.speaker: INTERVIEWER

audioscript.text: That is the end of section 2.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Today, I want to talk about self-regulatory focus theory, and how the actions of leaders can affect the way followers approach different situations.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Self-regulatory focus theory is a theory developed by Tori Higgins.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: He says that a person's focus at any given time is to either approach pleasure or avoid pain.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: These are two basic motivations that each and every one of us has, and they cause us to have different kinds of goals.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Promotion goals in different life situations emphasize achievement.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q31: The passage says *'Promotion goals in different life situations emphasize achievement'* — **'emphasize'** means **'focus on'**. So the answer is **achievement**.

audioscript.text: Prevention goals are oriented towards the avoidance of punishment.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: In a specific situation, our thoughts might focus more on promotion goals, or more on prevention goals.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The theory suggests that two factors affect which goals we are focusing on.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: First, there is a chronic factor.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: This factor is connected to a person's personality, and says that each person has a basic tendency to either focus more on promotion goals or focus more on prevention goals.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q32: The passage says the chronic factor *'is connected to a person's personality'* — **'comes from'** means **'is connected to'**. So the answer is **personality**.

audioscript.text: As part of his or her personality.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Second, there is a situational factor, which means that the context we are in can make us more likely to focus on one set of goals or the other.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q33: The passage says *'Second, there is a situational factor'* — this is the second factor that affects our focus. So the answer is **Situational**.

audioscript.text: For example, we are more likely to be thinking about pleasure and to have promotion goals when we are spending time with a friend.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q34: The passage says we have promotion goals *'when we are spending time with a friend'* — **'when with a'** means **'when we are spending time with'**. So the answer is **friend**.

audioscript.text: In contrast, if we are working on an important project for our boss, we are more likely to try to avoid making mistakes.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And therefore have more prevention goals in our mind.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Research has shown that the goals we are focusing on at a given time affect the way we think, for example, when focusing on promotion goals, people consider their ideal self.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q35: The passage says people with promotion focus consider *'their ideal self'* and then adds *'Their aspirations and gains'* — **'aspirations'** are things you hope to achieve. So the answer is **aspirations**.

audioscript.text: Their aspirations and gains.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q35: The passage says people with promotion focus consider *'their ideal self'* and then adds *'Their aspirations and gains'* — **'aspirations'** are things you hope to achieve. So the answer is **aspirations**.

audioscript.text: They don't think about what they can lose, so they think in a happier mode, they feel more inspired.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: To change.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: When people are focusing on prevention goals, they think about their ought self, what are they supposed to be?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: What are people expecting from them?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: They consider their obligations to others.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: As a result, they experience more anxiety and try to avoid situations.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Where they could lose.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Now that I have talked about the two focuses, and how they affect people, I want to look at the idea that the way leaders behave.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Or their style of leading can affect the focus that followers adopt in a specific situation.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q36: The passage says *'the way leaders behave, or their style of leading can affect the focus'* — **'behaviour'** and **'style'** are the two things that affect focus. So the answer is **style**.

audioscript.text: In talking about leadership, we often mention transformational leaders and transactional leaders.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Transformational leaders when interacting with their followers, focus on their development, in their words and actions, transformational leaders highlight change.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q37: The passage says transformational leaders *'focus on their development'* — **'pay special attention to'** means **'focus on'**. So the answer is **development**.

audioscript.text: Their speech is passionate and conveys a definitive vision.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q38: The passage says their speech *'conveys a definitive vision'* — **'passionately communicate a clear'** means **'conveys a definitive'**. So the answer is **vision**.

utterances.text: The theory suggests that two factors affect which goals we are focusing on.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: First, there is a chronic factor.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Section 2, you will hear a recorded talk giving an introduction to the historical theme park of Manchester River Port in England.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 15.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Welcome to Manham Port, where 1,000 years of history are brought to life.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: All the family can enjoy a day out at Manham.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Visit our copper mine.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: See models of the machinery it used, have your photo taken in 19th century costume, experience at first hand how people lived at different stages throughout history.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And especially how children studied, worked, and played.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The port of Manham is located in beautiful and peaceful countryside, on a bend in the great River Avon, and developed here because it's the highest navigable point of the Avon.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q11: The passage says the port developed because it was *'the highest navigable point of the Avon'* and a *'handy place to load and unload cargo'*. This means it was a good spot for boats on the river. So the answer is **B** — it was convenient for river transport.

audioscript.text: Boats can go no higher up this river, and proved a handy place to load and unload cargo to and from the sea, which is over 23 miles away.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q11: The passage says the port developed because it was *'the highest navigable point of the Avon'* and a *'handy place to load and unload cargo'*. This means it was a good spot for boats on the river. So the answer is **B** — it was convenient for river transport.

audioscript.text: A small port was already established here, when about 900 years ago, tin was discovered nearby.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Though it wasn't until the Industrial Revolution,
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: when a tremendous need for metals of all kinds developed, that Manham expanded to become one of the busiest ports in the country, and because it was already so busy.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q12: The passage says Manham expanded when *'a tremendous need for metals of all kinds developed'*. **'Tremendous need'** means a big **increase in demand**. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: Prospectors began to look for other minerals, and by the end of the nineteenth century, lead, copper, manganese and arsenic were added to the cargoes leaving Manham.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: In the early days, the ores had been smelted or processed in the same area they were mined.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But as demand grew, the smelting process required huge factory furnaces or fires.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: To melt the metal from the rock, and there was not enough coal in the local area, so the rocks containing minerals had to be shipped long distances.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q13: The passage explains that to melt metal, *'there was not enough coal in the local area'*. **Coal** is a **fuel**, so a **'not enough'** means a **shortage of fuel**. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: Sadly, in the 20th century, the great port of Manham declined, and thousands of workers were forced to emigrate out of the area.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q14: The passage says when the port declined, *'thousands of workers were forced to emigrate out of the area'*. **'Emigrate'** means to leave and go live somewhere else — they **went away**. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: The building at the port fell into disrepair.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And the place became almost forgotten, but then the Manham Trust was formed to conserve the historical resources of the area.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q15: The passage says the Trust was formed to *'conserve the historical resources'* and to *'set about reconstructing it'*. **'Reconstructing'** means to **rebuild** the port complex. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: It organized scores of local volunteers to remove undergrowth.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: To find the original outlines of the installations, it then brought in paid professionals to match installations with maps of the original port complex.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And to set about reconstructing it.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q15: The passage says the Trust was formed to *'conserve the historical resources'* and to *'set about reconstructing it'*. **'Reconstructing'** means to **rebuild** the port complex. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Today, you can see the results of this ambitious program of restoration.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The intention, and we believe this will be realized before the end of the year, is to return Manham Port.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: To the condition it reached at its peak, as the greatest copper port in the country.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 16 to 20.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 16 to 20.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: But what can you do and see on your visit today?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Here are just a few highlights.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: We suggest you start with the visit to the copper mine.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Travel on converted mining trains.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q16: The passage says you *'Travel on converted mining trains'* to go into the mountain. The question asks for specially adapted miners' what — the answer is **trains**.

audioscript.text: And journey into the depths of the mountain, along seams once worked by hundreds of miners.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Watch out especially for the great pumping machines which rid the mine of water.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But please be warned that like all mines, ours is very dark and closed in, and we do say that children under five, and also dogs should not be taken into the mine.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q17: The passage warns the mine is *'very dark and closed in'*. **'Closed in'** means **enclosed**. So the answer is **dark**.

audioscript.text: The next recommended visit is to the village school.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: While looking around the classrooms, take a special look at our display of games, which is one of the largest in the world.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q18: The passage says at the school, take a look at our *'display of games'*. A **'display'** is an **exhibition**. So the answer is **games**.

audioscript.text: And it's recommended that you time your visit to coincide with a guided tour.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q19: The passage says it's recommended you *'time your visit to coincide with a guided tour'*. So the recommended thing is a **guided tour**.

audioscript.text: This will give you the opportunity to ask lots of questions.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Near the school is the beautiful old sailing ketch called the George.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: You're welcome to board the boat and look round the cabins.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Look out for the ship's wheel, which was missing until only five years ago, when it was dredged out of the silt by a local fisherman.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: We have no idea how it got there, but it's been polished and proudly restored to its original place on the boat.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Please take care going down the ladders, if you wish to visit the lower deck.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q20: The passage says to take care going down the *'ladders'* and that children shouldn't *'use them'*. So children shouldn't use the **ladders**.

audioscript.text: We don't recommend you allow young children to use them.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q20: The passage says to take care going down the *'ladders'* and that children shouldn't *'use them'*. So children shouldn't use the **ladders**.

audioscript.text: So we hope you have a memorable visit to Manham Port, and will tell your friends all about us.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That is the end of Section 2.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.

audioscript.text: Today we're going to look at an important area of science, namely nanotechnology.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So, what is it?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Nano means tiny.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So it's science and engineering on the scale of atoms and molecules.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The idea is that by controlling and rearranging atoms, you can literally create anything.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: However, as we'll see, the science of the small has some big implications affecting us in many ways.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: There's no doubt that nanotechnology promises so much for civilization.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: However, all new technologies have their teething problems.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And with nanotechnology, society often gets the wrong idea about its capabilities.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q31: The passage says *'society often gets the wrong idea about its capabilities'* — **'gets the wrong idea'** means **'misunderstood'**. So the problem is that nanotechnology **is misunderstood by the public**. The answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Numerous science fiction books and movies have raised people's fears about nanotechnology.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: With scenarios such as inserting little nano-robots into your body that monitor everything you do without you realizing it, or self-replicating nano-robots that eventually take over the world.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So, how do we safeguard such a potentially powerful technology?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Some scientists recommend that nanoparticles be treated as new chemicals.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: With separate safety tests and clear labeling.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: They believe that greater care should also be taken with nanoparticles in laboratories and factories.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q32: The passage says *'greater care should also be taken with nanoparticles'* — **'greater care'** means **'more caution'**. So scientists believe nanoparticles **should be used with more caution**. The answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: Others have called for a withdrawal of new nano-products, such as cosmetics, and a temporary halt to many kinds of nanotech research.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But as far as I'm concerned, there's a need to plough ahead with the discoveries and applications of nanotechnology.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q33: The speaker says *'there's a need to plough ahead with the discoveries and applications'* — **'plough ahead'** means **'continue'**. So in her opinion, research **ought to be continued**. The answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: I really believe that most scientists would welcome a way to guard against unethical uses of such technology.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: We can't go around thinking that all innovation is bad, all advancement is bad.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: As with the debate about any new technology, it is how you use it that's important.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So, let's look at some of its possible uses.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Thanks to nanotechnology, there could be a major breakthrough in the field of transportation with the production of more durable metals.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q34: The passage says nanotechnology could lead to *'the production of more durable metals'* — **'durable'** means **'stronger'**. So the answer is **'metal'** or **'metals'**.

audioscript.text: These could be virtually unbreakable, lighter, and much more pliable.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Leading to planes that are 50 times lighter than at present.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Those same improved capabilities will dramatically reduce the cost of traveling into space.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: In terms of technology, the computer industry will be able to shrink computer parts down to minute sizes.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: We need nanotechnology.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: In order to create a new generation of computers that will work even faster, and will have a million times more memory, but will be about the size of a sugar cube.

audioscript.text: Nanotechnology could also revolutionize the way that we generate power.

audioscript.text: The cost of solar cells will be drastically reduced, so harnessing this energy will be far more economical than at present.

audioscript.text: But nanotechnology has much wider applications than this, and could have an enormous impact on our environment.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: For instance,

audioscript.text: tiny airborne nano-robots could be programmed to actually rebuild the ozone layer, which could lessen the impact of global warming on our planet.

audioscript.text: That's a pretty amazing thought, isn't it?

audioscript.text: On a more local scale, this new technology could help with the cleanup of environmental disasters, as nanotechnology will allow us to remove oil and other contaminants from the water far more effectively.

audioscript.text: And if nanotechnology progresses as expected, as a sort of building block set of about 90 atoms, then you could build anything you wanted from the bottom up.
